verses.text: In the 1611 King James Version of the Bible, you will find here a letter that looks to be a y with a superscript t. This rare yͭ glyph does not have its own Unicode, but is instead rendered by combining U+0079 and U+036D, and is to be read as an abbreviation of the word that: “…which was guide to them that took Iesus.” There are a total of 12 instances of this rare glyph in the 1611 King James Version. (See 1 John 1:1 for more.)
